# dsh-web-password-auth

Sign in to the DeepSeek Harness Web UI with a **username and password** instead of
the launch token.

Sessions persist across browser restarts until you sign out.
Optional TOTP two-factor authenticatio

essions persist across browser restarts until you sign out.
Optional TOTP two-factor authentication.
## What it does
| **Password sign-in** | First visit asks you to create an account; later visits ask for the passwor

d |
| **Persistent sessions** | A signed cookie keeps you signed in; no re-authentication per visit

|
| **Sign out** | Clears the cookie server-side (the cookie is `HttpOnly`, so only the Host can) |

| **Two-factor (optional)** | TOTP, compatible with any authenticator app |
| **Launch token kept**

| The `dsh web` URL still signs you in — it is the local fallback when you forget the password |
| *
*In-app settings page** | Settings → Security (安全): change the password, turn two-factor on or off,
gs page** | Settings → Security (安全): change the password, turn two-factor on or off, and sign out |
## Install

Then restart `dsh --profile web` and open the UI. The first visit shows
**Create your account**.

The plugin reads the Host's effective `cookieMaxAgeDays` from the Loader at startup and
**uses the s

maller of the two**. Without that, a mismatch would produce cookies the Host
rejects — sign-in would
look successful and then fail on every request.
### Making sessions last until sign-out

The Host caps cookie lifetime with `connection.cookieMaxAgeDays` (default 30). This
plugin's `sessio

nDays` must stay **at or under** that cap, or the Host rejects the
cookie with 401. To get year-long

sessions, raise both in your profile patch
(`$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Configuration
| Field | Default | Meaning |
| `sessionDays` | `365` | Browser session lifetime in days; must be ≤ `connection.cookieMaxAgeDays`

|
| `bootstrapLoopbackOnly` | `true` | Before an account exists, only this machine may create it |
|

`maxAttempts` | `5` | Failed sign-ins before the source address is locked out |
| `lockoutMs` | `30

0000` | Lockout duration in milliseconds |
| `minPasswordLength` | `8` | Rejected shorter passwords

|
| `totpIssuer` | `'DSH'` | Issuer name shown in authenticator apps |
| `totpAvailable` | `true` |
Offer two-factor enrolment on the account page |
## Host compatibility

The plugin never reads the frontend dist, never renders the index, and never claims the
`webServer`

fallback seat. It registers two exact routes (`/` and `/index.html`), checks the
session, and hands
an authenticated request to whichever fallback the Host installed.
Both fallback shapes the Host has shipped are supported:
| Host | Fallback type | Handled by |

| up to `0.2.1` | `(req, res) => void` | called directly |
| `0.2.2` and later | `{ resource(request
, peer) }` returning a Fetch `Response` | request built, resource called without a peer, response wr
eturning a Fetch `Response` | request built, resource called without a peer, response written back |

`set-cookie` is appended rather than overwritten, so launch-token exchange keeps every cookie
it ret
urns. Old and new Hosts run the same build.

If the Host registered no fallback at all, an authenticated request receives a readable 500.
The plu
gin fails closed: it never releases the shell unguarded.
## Where the password is stored

In the Harness credential store (`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`, mode 0600, written
under a cross-pro

redential store (`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`, mode 0600, written
under a cross-process file lock):

- `web-auth/password` — username plus a scrypt hash (`N=32768, r=8, p=1`, about
66 ms and 32 MB per

verification)
- `web-auth/totp` — base32 secret, enabled flag, and the last consumed time step

Plaintext passwords are never written anywhere. The signing key record
`client-connection/browser-se

ssion` is read but **never** written — its payload
format belongs to the Host.
## Creating the first account
There are two ways in, and both end at the same record:
| Situation | What happens |
| You open the plain URL (`http://127.0.0.1:3080/`, no `?token=`) and no account exists | The accoun

t-creation page renders. Submitting it writes the account and signs you in |
| You open the `?token=
...` URL `dsh web` prints | You are already signed in, so no page could be shown. **Settings → Secur
ity** offers "Create a password account" instead |

The second case is the common one, because the printed URL carries the token. Without that
in-panel

form the token would be a one-way door: you would have to hand-edit the `?token=`
parameter out of t
he URL to ever set a password.

Both paths are restricted to the machine running the harness while `bootstrapLoopbackOnly`
is on (th
e default), and both refuse once an account exists.

To start over, remove the `web-auth/password` record from `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml`;
the next vi
sit offers account creation again.
## Visual consistency

The Host-rendered pages cannot read `--dsw-alias-*`: the client stylesheet is not loaded
before sign

-in. They therefore carry the values behind those tokens as plain literals —
copied, not invented. A

previous revision used a blue primary button while the product's is
[该节后续省略]
## Security notes

- **Serve over TLS if anything but loopback can reach the port.** A password over
plain HTTP is read

able on the wire, and the launch token leaks through terminal
logs and process listings. Use `--tls-

cert`/`--tls-key`, or terminate TLS in a
reverse proxy.
- **Full permissions mean sign-in equals rem

ote code execution.** This plugin is
meant to sit in front of a `danger-full-access` composition. En

able two-factor
authentication if the port is reachable from anywhere you do not fully trust.
- **Ch

anging the password signs out every session.** The plugin deletes the
signing key record so all exis

ting cookies stop verifying. Per-session
revocation is not possible: the cookie payload format is ow

ned by the Host.
- **One user only.** Every authenticated browser shares the Host's owner principal;

the username is a label on one shared credential, not an account system.
- Failed sign-ins are coun

ted in memory per source address. A restart clears the
counters.
